output.best_reason: Version D has the most distinct voice and the most tension. Rosa's fear of the police has a period root (the village gendarme who takes your cow or your son), and her refusal to sit, her shaking hands, and the closing line about the glasses she left untouched give the scene an unsettled feel. Her memories of the discovery arrive as lived detail (the closed hand on the repeater, the mallet, the stairs taken too fast) rather than as a list. Version A is close behind: it is tighter, its clock explanation ("so I am never caught out") makes the fast clock a character trait, and Lina's shaking hands and Rosa's refusal to speak ill of anyone carry real suspicion. Version B is weaker for craft slips: the interviewer calls her "Madame Häfeli" while everyone else says Mademoiselle, a speaker tag is duplicated, and the clock facts are repeated almost word for word, so they read as recitation. Version C is flattest. It opens with "Good morning" in the middle of the night, its exposition is heavy ("Monsieur Monnier was found dead in his atelier this night"), and Rosa's voice is passive and generic, with little tension beyond the closing "Nothing was late."
